products.title: Drill Pipe Float Valve, Size 2F-3R (3-1/2″ Reg)
products.descriptionShort: Size 2F-3R drill pipe float valve for 3-1/2″ API Reg and 2-7/8″ API IF (box × pin) float subs. Model G and Model GA (flapper) from Crestex, Baker, Forum and Drillmax; valve OD 2-13/32 in.
products.descriptionLong:
A size 2F-3R drill pipe float valve sits in the float sub or bit sub above the bit and stops drilling fluid and cuttings flowing back up the string when circulation stops, when connections are made, and in a kick. Size 2F-3R fits subs cut with a 3-1/2″ API Reg and 2-7/8″ API IF (box × pin) connection. We supply it new in Model G and Model GA (flapper) from Crestex, Baker, Forum and Drillmax.

Makes and models in this size

MakeModelTypePart / cage no.
BakerModel GAFlapper, ported14423100N
CrestexModel GFlapper152-432
DrillmaxModel GFlapper1520433
DrillmaxModel GAFlapper, ported1520433
ForumModel GFlapper—
ForumModel GAFlapper, ported—

Part numbers are as cast on the valve cage or listed by the maker. Baker-pattern valves of the same size and model interchange in the same sub.

Models

  • Model G (flapper): Full-opening flapper that swings clear of the bore, for abrasive fluids and unrestricted flow.
  • Model GA (flapper, ported): Model G with a hardened 1/4 in tungsten-carbide orifice in the flapper, so differential pressure can be read at surface.

Dimensions

Valve outside diameter (D)2-13/32 in
Recess diameter in the sub (R = D + 1/32)2-7/16 in
Valve length (L)6-1/2 in
Baffle plate recess diameter (T)1-29/32 in
Valve bore, Model F1-9/16 in
Valve bore, Model G1-1/4 in

Models F and G share the same outside dimensions, so either fits the same float sub or bored-out drill collar.

Float sub connections

ConnectionTypical sub OD
3-1/2″ API Reg4-1/4″
2-7/8″ API IF (box × pin)4-1/8″

Running notes

  • Forum rates its Model F and G valves at 7,500 psi working pressure; we confirm the rating of other makes on the quotation.
  • If more than one float valve runs in the same string, space them apart.
  • Choose a ported model (FA or GA) when you need to read shut-in drill pipe pressure or want the string to fill partly while running in.

Ordering

Give the size, model and sub connection on your RFQ, and say whether you need the float sub or bit sub as well. We confirm lead time and documentation on the quotation.
products.seoTitle: 2F-3R Float Valve — Drill Pipe, Model G/GA
products.seoDescription: Size 2F-3R drill pipe float valve, Model G and Model GA, Crestex, Baker and Forum. Fits 3-1/2″ API Reg subs. Request a quote.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Model F, FA, G and GA?
faqs.answer: F and FA are plunger valves: a spring-loaded plunger gives positive shut-off, and FA adds a port for partial fill-up and pressure readings. G and GA are flapper valves: the flapper swings fully clear for an unrestricted bore, and GA adds a 1/4 in carbide orifice so differential pressure can be read at surface.

faqs.question: Which sub connection takes a size 2F-3R float valve?
faqs.answer: A float sub or bit sub with a 3-1/2″ API Reg and 2-7/8″ API IF (box × pin) connection, bored with a 2-7/16 in recess and a 1-29/32 in baffle plate recess.

faqs.question: How long is a size 2F-3R float valve?
faqs.answer: 6-1/2 in overall, with a 2-13/32 in outside diameter. The sub needs a 2-7/16 in recess to take it.

faqs.question: Can a Model F and a Model G run in the same sub?
faqs.answer: Yes. Forum's Model F and G valves have identical outside dimensions and use the same float sub or bored-out drill collar; only the bore through the valve differs.

faqs.question: What pressure are drill pipe float valves rated to?
faqs.answer: Forum rates its Model F and G float valves at 7,500 psi working pressure. We confirm the rating of the make you order on the quotation.

faqs.question: Are these float valves supplied new?
faqs.answer: Yes. We supply new valves to the size, model and make on your RFQ, and can quote the float sub and repair parts with them.

products.seoDescription: Size 6F drill pipe float valve, Model F. Fits 8-5/8″ API Reg subs. Request a quote.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Model F, FA, G and GA?
faqs.answer: F and FA are plunger valves: a spring-loaded plunger gives positive shut-off, and FA adds a port for partial fill-up and pressure readings. G and GA are flapper valves: the flapper swings fully clear for an unrestricted bore, and GA adds a 1/4 in carbide orifice so differential pressure can be read at surface.

faqs.question: Which sub connection takes a size 6F float valve?
faqs.answer: A float sub or bit sub with a 8-5/8″ API Reg, 6-5/8″ API FH and 6-5/8″ API IF connection, bored with a 5-23/32 in recess and a 5-3/16 in baffle plate recess.

faqs.question: How long is a size 6F float valve?
faqs.answer: 14-5/8 in overall, with a 5-11/16 in outside diameter. The sub needs a 5-23/32 in recess to take it.

faqs.question: Can a Model F and a Model G run in the same sub?
faqs.answer: Yes. Forum's Model F and G valves have identical outside dimensions and use the same float sub or bored-out drill collar; only the bore through the valve differs.

faqs.question: What pressure are drill pipe float valves rated to?
faqs.answer: Forum rates its Model F and G float valves at 7,500 psi working pressure. We confirm the rating of the make you order on the quotation.

faqs.question: Are these float valves supplied new?
faqs.answer: Yes. We supply new valves to the size, model and make on your RFQ, and can quote the float sub and repair parts with them.
